observation_summary: The addOrUpdate method in XYSeries fails with an IndexOutOfBoundsException when attempting to handle duplicate X values, because the existing logic assumes that a non-negative index from binarySearch always implies an update, failing to account for scenarios where duplicates are allowed.
reasoning_summary: The defect is in the procedural logic of the addOrUpdate method. The method uses binarySearch to find an index, but the subsequent logic incorrectly assumes that any non-negative index must be an update. When duplicates are allowed, the method needs to correctly navigate the list to either update or insert the new item. This is a procedural/algorithmic failure in how the series data is managed, rather than a simple missing guard or wrong initialization.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'The method addOrUpdate(Number x, Number y) was never modified to support this [duplicate X values], and therefore duplicate data were overwriting existing data.'
The stack trace shows an IndexOutOfBoundsException at line 564, which is inside the logic that handles the result of a search.
The code snippet at line 564 shows: 'this.data.add(-index - 1, new XYDataItem(x, y));', which is part of the algorithmic handling of the search result.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding conditions (e.g., checking allowDuplicateXValues), the core issue is the lack of a proper insertion algorithm for duplicates, not just a missing guard.
The capability to add/update exists; the logic for handling duplicates within that existing capability is flawed, which is an algorithmic issue.
